units.zh: 季布者，楚人也。
units.en: Ji Bu was a native of Chu.
units.literal: Ji Bu was a man of Chu.

units.zh: 為氣任俠，有名於楚。
units.en: A man of fierce spirit who lived as a knight-errant, he was famed throughout Chu.
units.literal: He was spirited and acted as a knight-errant, gaining great renown in Chu.

units.zh: 項籍使將兵，數窘漢王。
units.en: Xiang Ji appointed him to command troops, and on multiple occasions he drove the King of Han into desperate straits.
units.literal: Xiang Ji sent him to command troops, and he repeatedly put the Han King in dire straits.

units.zh: 及項羽滅，高祖購求布千金，敢有舍匿，罪及三族。
units.en: After the fall of Xiang Yu, Emperor Gaozu posted a bounty of a thousand gold pieces for Ji Bu's capture, decreeing that anyone who dared shelter or conceal him would have the punishment extended to three generations of their clan.
units.literal: When Xiang Yu was destroyed, Gaozu offered a thousand pieces of gold for Ji Bu's capture; anyone who dared harbor or conceal him would have the crime extend to three generations of his clan.

units.zh: 季布匿濮陽周氏。
units.en: Ji Bu went into hiding with the Zhou family in Puyang.
units.literal: Ji Bu hid with the Zhou family in Puyang.

units.zh: 周氏曰：「漢購將軍急，跡且至臣家，將軍能聽臣，臣敢獻計；
units.en: The Zhou family said, "The Han search for you, General, is urgent, and your trail will soon reach my house. If you, General, will heed me, I dare offer a plan;
units.literal: The Zhou family said, "The Han search for the general is urgent, and traces will soon reach my household. If the general can heed me, I dare offer a plan;

units.zh: 即不能，願先自剄。」
units.en: if not, I will slit my own throat first."
units.literal: if you cannot, I wish first to slit my own throat."

units.zh: 季布許之。
units.en: Ji Bu consented.
units.literal: Ji Bu agreed to this.

units.zh: 乃髡鉗季布，衣褐衣，置廣柳車中，并與其家僮數十人，之魯朱家所賣之。
units.en: They shaved Ji Bu's head, clamped an iron collar around his neck, dressed him in coarse cloth, and placed him in a broad-sided cart. Together with dozens of household slaves, they transported him to the estate of Zhu Jia in Lu and sold him there.
units.literal: They shaved Ji Bu's head, fitted him with an iron collar, dressed him in coarse hemp clothing, placed him in a wide willow cart, and along with several dozen of his household slaves, took him to be sold to Zhu Jia of Lu.

units.zh: 朱家心知是季布，乃買而置之田。
units.en: Zhu Jia secretly recognized that this was Ji Bu. He purchased him and set him to work in the fields.
units.literal: Zhu Jia recognized in his heart that this was Ji Bu, so he bought him and put him to work in the fields.

units.zh: 誡其子曰：「田事聽此奴，必與同食。」
units.en: He admonished his son, saying, "In the fields, take orders from this slave; you must eat at the same table with him."
units.literal: He admonished his son, saying, "In field affairs obey this slave; you must eat with him."

units.zh: 朱家乃乘軺車之洛陽，見汝陰侯滕公。
units.en: Zhu Jia then rode a light carriage to Luoyang, where he called upon Xiahou Ying, the Marquis of Ruyin.
units.literal: Zhu Jia then rode in a light carriage to Luoyang and saw the Marquis of Ruyin, Teng Gong.

units.zh: 滕公留朱家飲數日。
units.en: The Marquis kept Zhu Jia as his guest and drank with him for several days.
units.literal: Teng Gong detained Zhu Jia and feasted him for several days.

units.zh: 因謂滕公曰：「季布何大罪，而上求之急也？」
units.en: He then asked Teng Gong, "What grave offense has Ji Bu committed, for the Sovereign to pursue him with such urgency?"
units.literal: Then he said to Teng Gong, "What great crime has Ji Bu committed, that the Sovereign seeks him so urgently?"

units.zh: 滕公曰：「布數為項羽窘上，上怨之，故必欲得之。」
units.en: Teng Gong said, "Ji Bu repeatedly put the Sovereign in dire straits while serving Xiang Yu; the Sovereign resents him, and therefore is determined to capture him."
units.literal: Teng Gong said, "Ji Bu repeatedly put the Sovereign in dire straits while serving Xiang Yu; the Sovereign resents him, and therefore is determined to have him."

units.zh: 朱家曰：「君視季布何如人也？」
units.en: Zhu Jia said, 'What kind of man do you consider Ji Bu to be?'
units.literal: Zhu Jia said, 'What kind of man do you consider Ji Bu to be?'

units.zh: 曰：「賢者也。」
units.en: Teng Gong said, "A worthy man."
units.literal: He said, "A worthy man."

units.zh: 朱家曰：「臣各為其主用，季布為項籍用，職耳。
units.en: Zhu Jia said, 'Each minister serves his own lord. Ji Bu served Xiang Ji—that was merely his duty.
units.literal: Zhu Jia said, 'Each minister serves his own lord. Ji Bu served Xiang Ji—that was merely his duty.

units.zh: 項氏臣可盡誅邪？
units.en: Should all Xiang Yu's ministers be executed?
units.literal: Xiang clan ministers can all execute?

units.zh: 今上始得天下，獨以己之私怨求一人，何示天下之不廣也！
units.en: Now that the Sovereign has just won the empire, to hunt one man solely out of private resentment—what a display of narrow-mindedness to all under heaven!
units.literal: Now that the Sovereign has just obtained the empire, to seek one man solely out of private resentment—what a display of lack of magnanimity to all under heaven!

units.zh: 且以季布之賢而漢求之急如此，此不北走胡即南走越耳。
units.en: Moreover, with a man as worthy as Ji Bu sought by Han with such urgency, he will either flee north to the Xiongnu or south to the Yue.
units.literal: Moreover, with Ji Bu's worthiness and Han seek him urgent like this, this not north flee Hu then south flee Yue only.

units.zh: 夫忌壯士以資敵國，此伍子胥所以鞭荊平王之墓也。
units.en: To drive away stalwart warriors and thereby strengthen enemy states—this is why Wu Zixu whipped the tomb of King Ping of Chu.
units.literal: To drive away stalwart warriors and thereby aid enemy states—this is why Wu Zixu whipped the tomb of King Ping of Chu.

units.zh: 君何不從容為上言邪？」
units.en: Why not find a calm moment to speak to the Sovereign about this?"
units.literal: Why do you not speak to the Sovereign about this at your leisure?"

units.zh: 汝陰侯滕公心知朱家大俠，意季布匿其所，乃許曰：「諾。」
units.en: The Marquis of Ruyin, Teng Gong, knew in his heart that Zhu Jia was a great knight-errant, and suspected that Ji Bu was hiding in his home. He then agreed, saying, 'Very well.'
units.literal: Ruyin Hou Teng Gong heart knew Zhu Jia great knight-errant, suspected Ji Bu concealed his place, then promised said: 'Yes.'

units.zh: 待閒，果言如朱家指。
units.en: When he had a suitable moment, he spoke to the Emperor exactly as Zhu Jia had urged.
units.literal: He waited for a leisurely moment, and indeed spoke as Zhu Jia had directed.

units.zh: 上乃赦季布。
units.en: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Ji Bu.
units.literal: The Sovereign then pardoned Ji Bu.

units.zh: 當是時，諸公皆多季布能摧剛為柔，朱家亦以此名聞當世。
units.en: At that time, everyone praised Ji Bu for his ability to bend the unyielding and make it yielding, and Zhu Jia likewise won renown throughout the age for this.
units.literal: At this time, all the nobles praised Ji Bu for his ability to bend the unyielding and make it yielding, and Zhu Jia also gained fame in the present age through this.

units.zh: 季布召見，謝，上拜為郎中。
units.en: Ji Bu was summoned for an audience and expressed his gratitude. The Emperor appointed him as a Gentleman of the Palace.
units.literal: Ji Bu was summoned for an audience and expressed thanks. The Sovereign appointed him as a lang zhong (court attendant).

units.zh: 孝惠時，為中郎將。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Hui, he served as Commander of the Palace Guard.
units.literal: During Emperor Hui's reign, he served as zhong lang jiang (lieutenant general).

units.zh: 單于嘗為書嫚呂后，不遜，呂后大怒，召諸將議之。
units.en: The Chanyu once wrote a letter insulting Empress Lü in disrespectful terms. Empress Lü was greatly angered and summoned all the generals to discuss it.
units.literal: The Chanyu once wrote a letter insulting Empress Lü in disrespectful terms; Empress Lü was greatly angered and summoned the generals to discuss it.

units.zh: 上將軍樊噲曰：「臣願得十萬眾，橫行匈奴中。」
units.en: The Supreme General, Fan Kuai, said, 'I wish to obtain a force of 100,000 men and march unchecked through the Xiongnu lands.'
units.literal: Supreme General Fan Kuai said, "Your servant wishes to have a force of one hundred thousand and rampage through the Xiongnu lands."

units.zh: 諸將皆阿呂后意，曰「然」。
units.en: All the generals flattered Empress Lü's wishes and said, 'Yes.'
units.literal: Various generals all flattered Empress Lü's intention, said 'Yes'.

units.zh: 季布曰：「樊噲可斬也！
units.en: Ji Bu said, 'Fan Kuai should be executed!
units.literal: Ji Bu said: 'Fan Kuai can behead!

units.zh: 夫高帝將兵四十餘萬眾，困於平城，今噲柰何以十萬眾橫行匈奴中，面欺！
units.en: Indeed, when the Gao Emperor led over 400,000 troops, he was trapped at Pingcheng. Now how can Kuai march unchecked through the Xiongnu lands with 100,000 men? This is barefaced deception!
units.literal: Indeed Gao Emperor led troops forty more myriad multitude, trapped at Pingcheng, now Kuai how with ten myriad multitude rampage Xiongnu midst, face deceive!

units.zh: 且秦以事於胡，陳勝等起。
units.en: Moreover, when Qin was occupied with campaigns against the Hu, Chen Sheng and others rose in revolt.
units.literal: Moreover, when Qin was occupied with campaigns against the Hu, Chen Sheng and others rose up.

units.zh: 于今創痍未瘳，噲又面諛，欲搖動天下。」
units.en: Even now our wounds are not yet healed, yet Fan Kuai again flatters you to your face, wishing to shake the empire.'
units.literal: Even now our wounds are not yet healed, yet Kuai again flatters to your face, wishing to shake the empire.'

units.zh: 是時殿上皆恐，太后罷朝，遂不復議擊匈奴事。
units.en: At this, everyone in the hall fell silent with fear. The Empress Dowager dismissed the court, and the matter of attacking the Xiongnu was never raised again.
units.literal: At this time, all in the hall were terrified. The Empress Dowager dismissed the court, and they never again discussed attacking the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 季布為河東守，孝文時，人有言其賢者，孝文召，欲以為御史大夫。
units.en: Ji Bu was serving as the Governor of Hedong when, during the reign of Emperor Wen, certain people praised his worthiness. Emperor Wen summoned him, intending to appoint him as the Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Ji Bu served as governor of Hedong. During Emperor Wen's reign, people spoke of his worthiness, so Emperor Wen summoned him, intending to appoint him as Yushi Dafu (Censor-in-Chief).

units.zh: 復有言其勇，使酒難近。
units.en: But then others reported that although he was brave, he became belligerent when drunk and was difficult to deal with.
units.literal: Others again spoke of his bravery, but said that when he drank wine he was difficult to approach.

units.zh: 至，留邸一月，見罷。
units.en: Ji Bu arrived and was kept waiting at the state guesthouse for a month before being granted an audience and then dismissed.
units.literal: He arrived and was detained at the guesthouse for a month, then given an audience and dismissed.

units.zh: 季布因進曰：「臣無功竊寵，待罪河東。
units.en: Ji Bu then stepped forward and said, "Your servant has no merit yet has stealthily received favor, and stands awaiting punishment in Hedong.
units.literal: Ji Bu then advanced and said, "Your servant has no merit yet has stealthily received favor, and stands awaiting punishment in Hedong.

units.zh: 陛下無故召臣，此人必有以臣欺陛下者；
units.en: Your Majesty summoned me without cause—someone must have deceived Your Majesty about me;
units.literal: Your Majesty without cause summoned minister, this person must have with minister deceived Your Majesty;

units.zh: 今臣至，無所受事，罷去，此人必有以毀臣者。
units.en: Now I have arrived, received no duties, and been sent away—someone must have slandered me to Your Majesty.
units.literal: Now I have arrived and received no assignments, then been dismissed—this person must have slandered me.

units.zh: 夫陛下以一人之譽而召臣，一人之毀而去臣，臣恐天下有識聞之有以闚陛下也。」
units.en: If Your Majesty summons me because one man praises me and sends me away because one man slanders me, I fear that perceptive men throughout the empire, once they hear of it, will have reason to look into Your Majesty's judgment."
units.literal: For Your Majesty to summon me on one man's praise and send me away on one man's slander—I fear that the knowledgeable throughout the empire who hear of it will have grounds to scrutinize Your Majesty."

units.zh: 上默然慚，良久曰：「河東吾股肱郡，故特召君耳。」
units.en: The Emperor fell silent, ashamed; after a long while he said, "Hedong is my vital commandery, so I specially summoned you."
units.literal: The Sovereign fell silent, ashamed; after a long while he said, "Hedong is my arm-and-thigh commandery, so I specially summoned you."

units.zh: 布辭之官。
units.en: Ji Bu took his leave and returned to his post.
units.literal: Ji Bu took his leave and returned to his office.

units.zh: 楚人曹丘生，辯士，數招權顧金錢。
units.en: There was a man of Chu named Cao Qiu Sheng, a persuasive rhetorician who repeatedly sought influence and pursued gold and money.
units.literal: Cao Qiu Sheng of Chu was a persuasive rhetorician who repeatedly sought influence and pursued gold and money.

units.zh: 事貴人趙同等，與竇長君善。
units.en: He had attached himself to prominent figures such as Zhao Tong and was on friendly terms with Dou Changjun.
units.literal: He served noble persons like Zhao Tong and was on good terms with Dou Changjun.

units.zh: 季布聞之，寄書諫竇長君曰：「吾聞曹丘生非長者，勿與通。」
units.en: Ji Bu heard this and sent a letter admonishing Dou Changjun, saying, 'I have heard that Cao Qiu Sheng is not an upright person—do not associate with him.'
units.literal: Ji Bu heard this, sent letter admonished Dou Changjun said: 'I heard Cao Qiu Sheng not upright person, do not with communicate.'

units.zh: 及曹丘生歸，欲得書請季布。
units.en: When Cao Qiu returned home, he wished to obtain a letter of introduction to Ji Bu.
units.literal: When Cao Qiu Sheng returned, he wished to obtain a letter to request an introduction to Ji Bu.

units.zh: 竇長君曰：「季將軍不說足下，足下無往。」
units.en: Dou Changjun said, 'General Ji is not pleased with you—you should not go.'
units.literal: Dou Changjun said: 'Ji general not pleased you, you no go.'

units.zh: 固請書，遂行。
units.en: But he insisted on having the letter and set off regardless.
units.literal: He firmly requested the letter and then went.

units.zh: 使人先發書，季布果大怒，待曹丘。
units.en: He sent a messenger ahead with the letter. Ji Bu, as expected, flew into a rage and waited for Cao Qiu's arrival, ready to confront him.
units.literal: He sent someone to deliver the letter first, and Ji Bu indeed became greatly angered, waiting for Cao Qiu.

units.zh: 曹丘至，即揖季布曰：「楚人諺曰『得黃金百（斤），不如得季布一諾』，足下何以得此聲於梁楚閒哉？
units.en: Cao Qiu arrived and immediately bowed to Ji Bu, saying, 'The Chu people have a proverb: "Getting a hundred jin of yellow gold is not as good as getting one promise from Ji Bu." How did you, sir, obtain this reputation between Liang and Chu?
units.literal: Cao Qiu arrived, immediately bowed Ji Bu said: 'Chu people proverb says 'obtain yellow gold hundred (jin), not as obtain Ji Bu one promise', you sir how obtained this reputation in Liang Chu between?

units.zh: 且仆楚人，足下亦楚人也。
units.en: Besides, I am a man of Chu, and you too are a man of Chu.
units.literal: Moreover, I am a Chu person, and you, sir, are also a Chu person.

units.zh: 仆游揚足下之名於天下，顧不重邪？
units.en: I have traveled and spread your reputation throughout the empire—is this not a weighty matter?
units.literal: I travel spread you sir's name in tianxia, but not heavy?

units.zh: 何足下距仆之深也！」
units.en: Why do you, sir, reject me so deeply!'
units.literal: Why you sir reject I so deep!'

units.zh: 季布乃大說，引入，留數月，為上客，厚送之。
units.en: Ji Bu was greatly pleased. He invited Cao Qiu in, kept him as a guest for several months, treated him with the highest honor, and sent him off with lavish gifts.
units.literal: Ji Bu was then greatly pleased, led him in, detained him for several months, treated him as an honored guest, and richly sent him off.

units.zh: 季布名所以益聞者，曹丘揚之也。
units.en: The reason Ji Bu's reputation grew ever greater was that Cao Qiu had spread it far and wide.
units.literal: The reason Ji Bu's reputation became increasingly well-known was that Cao Qiu spread it.

units.zh: 季布弟季心，氣蓋關中，遇人恭謹，為任俠，方數千里，士皆爭為之死。
units.en: Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin possessed a spirit that overawed all Guanzhong. He treated others with respectful courtesy and lived as a knight-errant; across a region of several thousand li, gentlemen all competed for the chance to die on his behalf.
units.literal: Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin had a spirit that overshadowed all of Guanzhong. He treated people with respectful courtesy and lived as a knight-errant; within a region of several thousand li, gentlemen were all eager to die for him.

units.zh: 嘗殺人，亡之吳，從袁絲匿。
units.en: He once killed a man, fled to Wu, and took refuge with Yuan Si.
units.literal: He once killed a person, fled to Wu, and hid with Yuan Si.

units.zh: 長事袁絲，弟畜灌夫、籍福之屬。
units.en: For many years he served Yuan Si as an elder, while treating men such as Guan Fu and Ji Fu as younger brothers under his protection.
units.literal: He long served Yuan Si as to an elder, and treated men like Guan Fu and Ji Fu as younger brothers under his care.

units.zh: 嘗為中司馬，中尉郅都不敢不加禮。
units.en: He once served as a Palace Marshal, and even Zhi Du, the Commandant of Justice, did not dare treat him with anything less than full courtesy.
units.literal: He once served as zhong sima, and even the zhong wei Zhi Du dared not fail to show him proper respect.

units.zh: 少年多時時竊籍其名以行。
units.en: Young men of the day often invoked his name without permission to further their own ends.
units.literal: Young men often secretly borrowed his name from time to time to carry out their affairs.

units.zh: 當是時，季心以勇，布以諾，著聞關中。
units.en: In those days, Ji Xin was celebrated for his courage and Ji Bu for the reliability of his word—both were famous throughout Guanzhong.
units.literal: At this time, Ji Xin was known for bravery and Ji Bu for keeping his word—their reputations were prominent throughout Guanzhong.

units.zh: 季布母弟丁公，為楚將。
units.en: Ji Bu's mother's younger brother Ding Gong served as a Chu general.
units.literal: Ji Bu mother's younger brother Ding Gong, served as Chu general.

units.zh: 丁公為項羽逐窘高祖彭城西，短兵接，高祖急，顧丁公曰：「兩賢豈相戹哉！」
units.en: Ding Gong, serving Xiang Yu, pursued and cornered Emperor Gaozu west of Pengcheng. They met in close combat; the Emperor was in peril and looked back at Ding Gong, saying, "How can two worthy men afflict each other!"
units.literal: Ding Gong, serving Xiang Yu, pursued and cornered Gaozu west of Pengcheng. They met in close combat; Gaozu was in peril and looked back at Ding Gong, saying, "How can two worthy men afflict each other!"

units.zh: 於是丁公引兵而還，漢王遂解去。
units.en: At this, Ding Gong withdrew his troops, and the King of Han was able to escape.
units.literal: So Ding Gong led his troops back, and the Han King thus escaped.

units.zh: 及項王滅，丁公謁見高祖。
units.en: After the fall of Xiang Yu, Ding Gong sought an audience with Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: When Xiang Yu was destroyed, Ding Gong went for an audience with Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖以丁公徇軍中，曰：「丁公為項王臣不忠，使項王失天下者，乃丁公也。」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu had Ding Gong paraded through the army and said, "Ding Gong served King Xiang as a minister without loyalty; the one who caused King Xiang to lose the empire is Ding Gong."
units.literal: Gaozu had Ding Gong paraded through the army and said, "Ding Gong served as King Xiang's minister without loyalty; the one who caused King Xiang to lose the empire is Ding Gong."

units.zh: 遂斬丁公，曰：「使後世為人臣者無效丁公！」
units.en: Gaozu then had Ding Gong beheaded, saying, "Let no minister in later generations follow Ding Gong's example!"
units.literal: He then beheaded Ding Gong, saying, "Let no minister in future generations imitate Ding Gong!"

units.zh: 欒布者，梁人也。
units.en: Luan Bu was a native of Liang.
units.literal: Luan Bu was a man of Liang.

units.zh: 始梁王彭越為家人時，嘗與布游。
units.en: In the early days, when Peng Yue—who would later become King of Liang—was still a commoner, he and Luan Bu had been companions.
units.literal: When the Liang King Peng Yue was still a commoner, he once roamed with Bu.

units.zh: 窮困，賃傭於齊，為酒人保。
units.en: Destitute, Luan Bu hired himself out as a laborer in Qi and worked as a guard at a tavern.
units.literal: He was impoverished and distressed, hired himself out as labor in Qi, and served as security at a tavern.

units.zh: 數歲，彭越去之巨野中為盜，而布為人所略賣，為奴於燕。
units.en: After several years, Peng Yue departed for the Juye marshes to become a bandit, while Luan Bu was kidnapped and sold into slavery in Yan.
units.literal: After several years, Peng Yue went into the Juye marshes to become a bandit, while Bu was abducted and sold by people, becoming a slave in Yan.

units.zh: 為其家主報仇，燕將臧荼舉以為都尉。
units.en: He avenged his master's death, and the Yan general Zang Tu, impressed, recommended him to the rank of District Commandant.
units.literal: He avenged his household master, and the Yan general Zang Tu recommended him to serve as du wei.

units.zh: 臧荼後為燕王，以布為將。
units.en: When Zang Tu later became King of Yan, he appointed Luan Bu as one of his generals.
units.literal: Zang Tu later became King of Yan and appointed Bu as his general.

units.zh: 及臧荼反，漢擊燕，虜布。
units.en: When Zang Tu rebelled, the Han forces attacked Yan and took Luan Bu prisoner.
units.literal: When Zang Tu rebelled, Han attacked Yan and captured Bu.

units.zh: 梁王彭越聞之，乃言上，請贖布以為梁大夫。
units.en: When the King of Liang, Peng Yue, heard of this, he petitioned the Emperor to ransom Luan Bu and appoint him as a Minister of Liang.
units.literal: The Liang King Peng Yue heard this and then spoke to the Sovereign, requesting to redeem Bu to serve as a Liang daifu (minister).

units.zh: 使於齊，未還，漢召彭越，責以謀反，夷三族。
units.en: Luan Bu was sent on a diplomatic mission to Qi and had not yet returned when the Han court summoned Peng Yue, charged him with plotting rebellion, and exterminated his three clans.
units.literal: He was sent on a mission to Qi and had not yet returned when Han summoned Peng Yue, blamed him for plotting rebellion, and exterminated his three clans.

units.zh: 已而梟彭越頭於雒陽下，詔曰：「有敢收視者，輒捕之。」
units.en: Soon after, Peng Yue's head was displayed below Luoyang, and an edict said, "Anyone who dares to gather or look upon it will be arrested at once."
units.literal: Soon Peng Yue's head was displayed below Luoyang, and an edict said, "Anyone who dares to gather or look upon it will be arrested at once."

units.zh: 布從齊還，奏事彭越頭下，祠而哭之。
units.en: When Luan Bu returned from Qi, he reported on his mission beneath Peng Yue's severed head, made offerings, and wept for him.
units.literal: When Bu returned from Qi, he reported on his mission beneath Peng Yue's head, made offerings, and wept for him.

units.zh: 吏捕布以聞。
units.en: The officials arrested Luan Bu and reported the matter to the throne.
units.literal: The officials captured Bu and reported it.

units.zh: 上召布，罵曰：「若與彭越反邪？
units.en: The Emperor summoned Luan Bu and cursed him, saying, "Did you rebel with Peng Yue?
units.literal: The Sovereign summoned Bu and cursed him, saying, "Did you rebel with Peng Yue?

units.zh: 吾禁人勿收，若獨祠而哭之，與越反明矣。
units.en: I forbade anyone to attend to his remains, yet you alone made offerings and wept for him—it is clear you were part of Yue's rebellion.
units.literal: I prohibited people from collecting it, but you alone sacrificed and wept for him—it's clear you rebelled with Yue.

units.zh: 趣亨之。」
units.en: Hurry and execute him.'
units.literal: Hurry execute him.'

units.zh: 方提趣湯，布顧曰：「願一言而死。」
units.en: Just as they were leading him to hurry to the cauldron, Bu looked back and said, 'I wish to speak one word before I die.'
units.literal: Just as they were leading him in haste to the cauldron, Bu looked back and said, "I wish to speak one word before I die."

units.zh: 上曰：「何言？」
units.en: The Sovereign said, 'What words?'
units.literal: Sovereign said: 'What words?'

units.zh: 布曰：「方上之困於彭城，敗滎陽、成皋閒，項王所以（遂）不能［遂］西，徒以彭王居梁地，與漢合從苦楚也。
units.en: Bu said, 'When the Sovereign was distressed at Pengcheng and defeated between Xingyang and Chenggao, the reason Xiang Yu could not advance west was only because the Peng King dwelt in Liang lands and allied with Han to afflict Chu.
units.literal: Bu said: 'Just Sovereign's distress at Pengcheng, defeated between Xingyang, Chenggao, Xiang Wang reason not able west, only because Peng King dwelt Liang lands, with Han allied together afflicted Chu.

units.zh: 當是之時，彭王一顧，與楚則漢破，與漢而楚破。
units.en: At that moment, the fate of the empire hung on a single decision by the King of Peng: had he sided with Chu, Han would have been destroyed; because he sided with Han, Chu was destroyed.
units.literal: At this time, with just one glance from the Peng King, if he allied with Chu then Han would be broken, if he allied with Han then Chu would be broken.

units.zh: 且垓下之會，微彭王，項氏不亡。
units.en: Moreover, at the battle of Gaixia, without the King of Peng, the house of Xiang would never have fallen.
units.literal: Moreover, at the Gaixia meeting, without the Peng King, the Xiang clan would not have perished.

units.zh: 天下已定，彭王剖符受封，亦欲傳之萬世。
units.en: After the empire was settled, the King of Peng received his tally and his fief, and naturally wished to pass them down for ten thousand generations.
units.literal: The empire was already settled, the Peng King had his tally divided and received his fief, and he also wished to transmit it to ten thousand generations.

units.zh: 今陛下一徵兵於梁，彭王病不行，而陛下疑以為反，反形未見，以苛小案誅滅之，臣恐功臣人人自危也。
units.en: Now Your Majesty levied troops from Liang just once, and when the King of Peng was too ill to comply, Your Majesty suspected him of rebellion. No evidence of rebellion was ever found, yet he was destroyed on a trivial pretext. I fear that every minister who has rendered meritorious service now feels his own life is in danger.
units.literal: Now Your Majesty summoned troops just once from Liang, the Peng King was ill and did not go, yet Your Majesty suspected him of rebellion. The shape of rebellion was not seen, but you exterminated him with a harsh and petty case. I fear all the merit ministers will each feel endangered.

units.zh: 今彭王已死，臣生不如死，請就亨。」
units.en: Now that the Peng King is already dead, living is not as good as dying for me. Please proceed with the boiling.'
units.literal: Now Peng King already dead, minister living not as dying, please proceed boil.'

units.zh: 於是上乃釋布罪，拜為都尉。
units.en: Thereupon the Emperor released Luan Bu from guilt and appointed him District Commandant.
units.literal: Thereupon the Sovereign released Bu from guilt and appointed him District Commandant.

units.zh: 孝文時，為燕相，至將軍。
units.en: During the reign of Emperor Wen, he served as the Chancellor of Yan and eventually rose to the rank of general.
units.literal: During Emperor Wen's reign, he served as prime minister of Yan and rose to the rank of general.

units.zh: 布乃稱曰：「窮困不能辱身下志，非人也；
units.en: Bu then declared, 'If poverty and distress cannot humiliate one's self or lower one's ambitions, that is not human;
units.literal: Bu then declared: 'Impoverished distressed cannot humiliate self lower ambitions, not person;

units.zh: 富貴不能快意，非賢也。」
units.en: If wealth and nobility cannot delight one's intentions, that is not worthy.'
units.literal: Wealth nobility cannot delight intentions, not worthy.'

units.zh: 於是嘗有德者厚報之，有怨者必以法滅之。
units.en: From then on, he repaid generously all those who had once shown him kindness, and those who had wronged him he invariably destroyed through the law.
units.literal: So he thickly repaid those who had once shown him virtue, and those who had grievances against him he certainly extinguished with the law.

units.zh: 吳（軍）［楚］反時，以軍功封俞侯，復為燕相。
units.en: During the time of the Wu [Chu] rebellion, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yu for military merit, and again served as prime minister of Yan.
units.literal: Wu (army) [Chu] rebellion time, with military merit enfeoffed Yu Hou, again served as Yan prime minister.

units.zh: 燕齊之閒皆為欒布立社，號曰欒公社。
units.en: Throughout the lands between Yan and Qi, the people established shrines in his honor, calling them the Shrines of Lord Luan.
units.literal: Between Yan and Qi, all established shrines for Luan Bu, calling them the Luan Gong shrines.

units.zh: 景帝中五年薨。
units.en: He died in the fifth year of the Zhongyuan reign of Emperor Jing.
units.literal: In the fifth year of the Zhongyuan reign of Emperor Jing, he died.

units.zh: 子賁嗣，為太常，犧牲不如令，國除。
units.en: His son Ben inherited the title and served as the Grand Master of Ceremonies, but because the sacrificial animals he provided did not meet the prescribed standards, his fief was abolished.
units.literal: His son Ben succeeded him and served as Grand Master of Ceremonies, but his sacrifices did not conform to regulations, so his fief was eliminated.

units.zh: 太史公曰：以項羽之氣，而季布以勇顯於楚，身屨（典）軍搴旗者數矣，可謂壯士。
units.en: The Grand Historian said: In the age of Xiang Yu's fierce power, Ji Bu became renowned in Chu for his bravery; he personally commanded troops and seized enemy banners several times. He can indeed be called a stalwart warrior.
units.literal: The Grand Historian said: Under Xiang Yu's authority, Ji Bu nonetheless became famed in Chu for bravery; he personally led troops and seized enemy banners on several occasions—he may be called a stalwart warrior.

units.zh: 然至被刑戮，為人奴而不死，何其下也！
units.en: Yet when he reached the point of punishment and branding, became another man's slave, and still did not die, how low he sank!
units.literal: Yet when it came to suffering punishment and branding, becoming another man's slave and not dying—how base!

units.zh: 彼必自負其材，故受辱而不羞，欲有所用其未足也，故終為漢名將。
units.en: He must have been confident in his own abilities, and therefore accepted humiliation without shame, knowing that his talents had not yet been fully employed. In the end, he became one of the celebrated generals of Han.
units.literal: He certainly relied upon his own talents, therefore accepted humiliation without feeling shame, wishing to have some use for what was still insufficient, and therefore finally became a famous general of Han.

units.zh: 賢者誠重其死。
units.en: A truly worthy man weighs his death carefully.
units.literal: Truly, the worthy value their death.

units.zh: 夫婢妾賤人感慨而自殺者，非能勇也，其計畫無復之耳。
units.en: When slave girls, concubines, and people of low station kill themselves in a moment of passion, it is not because they are brave—it is because they see no way forward.
units.literal: Indeed, when concubines and base people are emotionally moved and commit suicide, it is not that they are able to be brave—their plans simply have no recovery.

units.zh: 欒布哭彭越，趣湯如歸者，彼誠知所處，不自重其死。
units.en: When Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue and walked toward the boiling cauldron as calmly as if he were going home, it was because he truly understood his situation and did not cling to his own life.
units.literal: Luan Bu wept for Peng Yue and hurried to the cauldron as if returning home—he truly knew his situation and did not value his own death.

units.zh: 雖往古烈士，何以加哉！
units.en: Even among the fierce warriors of antiquity, who could surpass this?
units.literal: Even the martyred warriors of old—how could one surpass this!

units.zh: 漢則馬遷、蕭望，晉則裴楷、張華。
units.en: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.
units.literal: In Han there were Sima Qian and Xiao Wangzhi; in Jin there were Pei Kai and Zhang Hua.

units.zh: 帝又怒曰：「爾自作范增，以我為項羽邪！」
units.en: The emperor raged again. "You make yourself Fan Zeng and call me Xiang Yu!"
units.literal: The emperor was angry again and said, "You make yourself Fan Zeng and take me for Xiang Yu!"

units.zh: 珽曰：「項羽人身亦何由可及，但天命不至耳。
units.en: Ting said, "Xiang Yu as a man—who could match him? Only Heaven's mandate never came.
units.literal: Ting said, "Xiang Yu as a man—how could he be reached? Only Heaven's mandate did not arrive.

units.zh: 項羽布衣，率烏合衆，五年而成霸王業。
units.en: Xiang Yu in plain cloth led a rabble army and in five years built a hegemon's realm.
units.literal: Xiang Yu in plain cloth led a rabble host and in five years achieved the hegemon's enterprise.

units.zh: 陛下藉父兄資，財得至此，臣以項羽未易可輕。
units.en: Your Majesty, on your father's and brother's capital, reached only this. I say Xiang Yu is not to be despised lightly.
units.literal: Your Majesty by your father's and elder brother's resources attained only to this; your servant holds that Xiang Yu is not lightly to be despised.

units.zh: 群臣從至，上議曰：「丞相臣平、太尉臣勃、大將軍臣武、御史大夫臣蒼、宗正臣郢、朱虛侯臣章、東牟侯臣興居、典客臣揭再拜言大王足下：子弘等皆非孝惠皇帝子，不當奉宗廟。
units.en: The ministers followed and arrived. The court deliberated, saying: "Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, General-in-Chief Chai Wu, Grandee Secretary Zhang Cang, Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Ying, Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang, Marquis Dong Mou Liu Xingju, and Court Receptionist Liu Jie bowed twice and addressed Your Majesty: Zi Hong and the others are not sons of Emperor Xiaohui and should not serve at the ancestral temple.
units.literal: The ministers followed and arrived. The court deliberated, saying: "Chancellor Chen Ping, Grand Commandant Zhou Bo, General-in-Chief Chai Wu, Grandee Secretary Zhang Cang, Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Ying, Marquis Zhu Xu Liu Zhang, Marquis Dong Mou Liu Xingju, and Court Receptionist Liu Jie bowed twice and addressed Your Majesty: Zi Hong and the others are not sons of Emperor Xiaohui and ought not serve at the ancestral temple.

units.zh: 二月，出孝惠皇帝後宮美人，令得嫁。
units.en: In the second month, he released the palace ladies from Emperor Hui's harem and allowed them to marry.
units.literal: Second month, he released the beautiful women from the harem of Emperor Hui and permitted them to marry.

units.zh: 高祖，沛豐邑中陽里人也，姓劉氏。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was born in Zhongyang Village in the town of Fengyi, Pei County. His surname was Liu.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was a person of Zhongyang Village, Fengyi Town, Pei County, and his surname was Liu.

units.zh: 蕭何曰：「劉季固多大言，少成事。」
units.en: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji certainly talks big but accomplishes little."
units.literal: Xiao He said: "Liu Ji indeed makes many big claims, accomplishes few matters."

units.zh: 秦二年十月，沛公攻胡陵、方與，還守豐。
units.en: In the tenth month of the second year of Qin, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, then returned to defend Feng.
units.literal: Qin second year tenth month, Pei Gong attacked Hu Ling and Fang Yu, returned to defend Feng.

units.zh: 呂公曰：「臣少好相人，相人多矣，無如季相，願季自愛。
units.en: Lü Gong said: "Since I was young, I've enjoyed reading faces. I've read many people's faces, but none compare to Ji's. I hope Ji takes good care of himself.
units.literal: Lü Gong said: "I from youth favored physiognomy, have read many people's faces, none like Ji's appearance, wish Ji to take care of himself.

units.zh: 臣有息女，願為箕帚妾。」
units.en: I have a young daughter and wish to make her Ji's humble servant."
units.literal: I have a young daughter, wish to make her Ji's broom and dustpan servant."

units.zh: 沛令善公，求之不與，何自妄許與劉季？」
units.en: The magistrate of Pei was your friend and asked for her, but you wouldn't give her. Why are you now rashly promising her to Liu Ji?"
units.literal: The Pei magistrate was friendly with you, requested her and you did not give, why now rashly promise her to Liu Ji?"

units.zh: 呂后曰：「季所居上常有雲氣，故從往常得季。」
units.en: Empress Lü said: "There are always clouds above where you stay. That's why we can always find you by following them."
units.literal: Empress Lu said: 'Where Ji resides above constantly has cloud aura, therefore following it constantly finds Ji.'

units.zh: 諸父老皆曰：「平生所聞劉季奇怪，當貴，且卜筮之，莫如劉季最吉。」
units.en: All the elders said: "In our lifetimes we have heard that Liu Ji is strange and marked for nobility. Moreover, when we divined on it, none was more auspicious than Liu Ji."
units.literal: All the elders said: 'In our lives we have heard Liu Ji is strange and extraordinary, should be noble, moreover divining it, none is more auspicious than Liu Ji.'

units.zh: 已而有娠，遂產高祖。
units.en: Soon after, she became pregnant and gave birth to Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Soon after she became pregnant, and then gave birth to the Supreme Ancestor.

units.zh: 高祖為人，隆準而龍顏，美須髯，左股有七十二黑子。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu had a prominent nose, a face like a dragon, beautiful whiskers and beard, and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor as a person had a high nose and dragon face, beautiful beard and whiskers, and on his left thigh there were seventy-two black moles.

units.zh: 高祖每酤留飲，酒讎數倍。
units.en: Whenever Emperor Gaozu bought wine, he stayed to drink, and the bill was several times higher.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor each time he bought wine would stay and drink, the wine price several times.

units.zh: 高祖常繇咸陽，縱觀秦皇帝，喟然大息，曰：「嗟乎，大丈夫當如此矣！」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu often passed through Xianyang and gazed upon the Qin emperor. He would sigh deeply and say: "Ah, this is how a true man should live!"
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor often performed corvée service at Xianyang and was allowed to observe the Qin emperor; he sighed deeply and said: "Alas, a great man should be like this!"

units.zh: 高祖為亭長，素易諸吏，乃紿為謁曰「賀錢萬」，實不持一錢。
units.en: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu had always treated the officials lightly. He deceived them by having the announcement read "Congratulatory gift: ten thousand cash," though in fact he did not bring a single coin.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor was pavilion chief, usually casual with the officials, then deceived to make the announcement saying "Congratulatory money ten thousand," in reality he did not bring a single cash.

units.zh: 呂公者，好相人，見高祖狀貌，因重敬之，引入坐上坐。
units.en: Lü Gong was skilled in reading faces. When he saw Emperor Gaozu's appearance, he was greatly impressed and led him inside to be seated in the place of honor.
units.literal: Lü Gong was good at physiognomy, saw the Supreme Ancestor's appearance, because of this greatly respected him, led him in to sit in the seat of honor.

units.zh: 高祖因狎侮諸客，遂坐上坐，無所詘。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu took advantage of this to treat all the guests with casual familiarity and even insult them. He sat in the place of honor without showing any humility.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor because of this treated the various guests with familiarity and insult, then sat in the seat of honor, was not humble in any way.

units.zh: 酒闌，呂公因目固留高祖。
units.en: As the banquet ended, Lü Gong signaled insistently to keep Emperor Gaozu there.
units.literal: The wine came to an end, Lü Gong because of this gave meaningful looks and firmly kept the Supreme Ancestor.

units.zh: 卒與高祖。
units.en: In the end, she married Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: In the end he married with the Supreme Ancestor.

units.zh: 高祖嘗告歸之田。
units.en: Once, Emperor Gaozu requested leave to return to his fields.
units.literal: The Supreme Ancestor once requested leave to return to the fields.

units.zh: 老父已去，高祖適從旁舍來，呂后具言客有過，相我子母皆大貴。
units.en: The old man had already left. Emperor Gaozu had just returned from a neighboring house. Empress Lü told him everything: a guest had passed by and read the faces of her, the children, and her mother—they were all greatly noble.
units.literal: The old man had already left; Gaozu had just come from the neighboring house. Empress Lü told him in full that a guest had passed by and read the faces of her and her children—all were greatly noble.

units.zh: 高祖問，曰：「未遠。」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu asked where the old man had gone. She said, "Not far."
units.literal: Gaozu asked, said: 'Not far.'

units.zh: 高祖乃謝曰：「誠如父言，不敢忘德。」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu then thanked him and said: "If what you say is true, I won't forget your kindness."
units.literal: Gaozu then thanked saying: 'Truly as father says, do not dare forget the kindness.'

units.zh: 及高祖貴，遂不知老父處。
units.en: When Emperor Gaozu rose to power, he could no longer find the old man.
units.literal: When Gaozu became noble, then did not know the old father's whereabouts.

units.zh: 高祖為亭長，乃鲈竹皮為冠，令求盜之薛治，時時冠之，及貴常冠，所謂「劉氏冠」也。
units.en: While he was pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu made a cap of bamboo sheathing. When he was sent to pursue bandits in the Xue district he wore it from time to time, and after he rose high he still wore it constantly. This is what was called the "Liu family cap."
units.literal: While Gaozu was pavilion chief, he made a cap of bamboo sheathing; he was ordered to pursue bandits in the Xue district and wore it from time to time; after he rose high he still wore it constantly—this is what is called the "Liu family cap."

units.zh: 高祖以亭長為縣送徒驪山，徒多道亡。
units.en: As pavilion chief, Emperor Gaozu was assigned by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li. Many of the convicts fled along the road.
units.literal: Gaozu as pavilion chief was ordered by the county to escort convicts to Mount Li, the convicts many fled on the road.

units.zh: 高祖被酒，夜徑澤中，令一人行前。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and at night went directly through the marsh, ordering one man to go ahead.
units.literal: Gaozu was drunk, at night went straight through the marshes, ordered one person to go ahead.

units.zh: 高祖醉，曰：「壯士行，何畏！」
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was drunk and said: "A brave man walks on. What is there to fear!"
units.literal: Gaozu was drunk, said: 'A brave man walks forward, what is there to fear!'

units.zh: 後人至，高祖覺。
units.en: Later people arrived, and Emperor Gaozu woke up.
units.literal: Later people arrived, Gaozu awoke.

units.zh: 告高祖，高祖乃心獨喜，自負。
units.en: They told Emperor Gaozu, who was secretly delighted and grew confident in himself.
units.literal: Told Gaozu, Gaozu then in his heart alone rejoiced, considered himself superior.

units.zh: 高祖隱於芒、碭山澤間，呂后與人俱求，常得之。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang. Empress Lü and others searched for him together and always found him.
units.literal: Gaozu hid in the mountains and marshes between Mang and Dang, Empress Lu and others together sought him, constantly found him.

units.zh: 高祖怪問之。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was surprised and asked how.
units.literal: Gaozu strangely questioned her.

units.zh: 高祖又喜。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu was delighted once more.
units.literal: Gaozu again was happy.

units.zh: 乃令樊噲召高祖。
units.en: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.
units.literal: He then ordered Fan Kuai to summon Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖之眾已數百人矣。
units.en: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.
units.literal: Gaozu's following already numbered several hundred men.

units.zh: 於是樊噲從高祖來。
units.en: So Fan Kuai came to follow Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Therefore Fan Kuai followed Gaozu and came.

units.zh: 蕭、曹恐，踰城保高祖。
units.en: Xiao and Cao were afraid, so they climbed over the wall to join Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Xiao and Cao feared, climbed over the wall to protect Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖乃書帛射城上，與沛父老曰：「天下同苦秦久矣。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, saying to the elders of Pei: "All under heaven have suffered under Qin for a long time.
units.literal: Gaozu then wrote on silk and shot it onto the city wall, telling the Pei elders: 'The world together has suffered under Qin for a long time.

units.zh: 父老乃帥子弟共殺沛令，開城門迎高祖，欲以為沛令。
units.en: The elders then led the young men together to kill the magistrate of Pei, opened the city gates to welcome Emperor Gaozu, and wanted to make him magistrate of Pei.
units.literal: The elders then led the young men together to kill the Pei magistrate, opened the city gates to welcome Gaozu, wished to make him Pei magistrate.

units.zh: 高祖曰：「天下方擾，諸侯並起，令置將不善，一敗塗地。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu said: "The world is in chaos right now, with feudal lords rising up everywhere. If you appoint a commander who is not capable, one defeat will ruin everything.
units.literal: Gaozu said: 'The world is currently in chaos, feudal lords all rise, if the magistrate appoints generals poorly, one defeat and all lost.

units.zh: 蕭、曹等皆文吏，自愛，恐事不就，後秦種族其家，盡讓高祖。
units.en: Xiao, Cao, and the others were all civil officials who cherished themselves. They feared that if things didn't succeed, Qin would exterminate their families, so they all yielded to Emperor Gaozu.
units.literal: Xiao, Cao and others all were civil officials, cherished themselves, feared the matter would not succeed, afterward Qin would exterminate their families, all yielded to Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖數讓。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu declined repeatedly.
units.literal: Gaozu repeatedly declined.

units.zh: 眾莫肯為，高祖乃立為沛公。
units.en: No one else was willing to take it, so Emperor Gaozu was established as Lord of Pei.
units.literal: The crowd none would do it, Gaozu then was established as Pei Gong.

units.zh: 十一月，沛公引兵之薛。
units.en: In the eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xue.
units.literal: Eleventh month, Pei Gong led troops to Xi.

units.zh: 秦泗川守壯兵敗於薛，走至戚，沛公左司馬得殺之。
units.en: The Qin governor of Si River Zhuang was defeated at Xue and fled to Qi, where Pei Gong's left commander Sima De killed him.
units.literal: Qin Sishui defender Zhuang's troops defeated at Xue, fled to Qi, Pei Gong's left marshal captured and killed him.

units.zh: 沛公還軍亢父，至方與。
units.en: Pei Gong returned his army to Kangfu and arrived at Fang Yu.
units.literal: Pei Gong returned his army to Kang Fu, arrived at Fang Yu.

units.zh: 雍齒雅不欲屬沛公，及魏招之，即反為魏守豐。
units.en: Yong Chi had long not wanted to serve Pei Gong, and when Wei summoned him, he immediately rebelled and defended Feng for Wei.
units.literal: Yong Chi usually did not wish to belong to Pei Gong, when Wei summoned him, immediately rebelled to guard Feng for Wei.

units.zh: 沛公攻豐，不能取。
units.en: Pei Gong attacked Feng but could not capture it.
units.literal: Pei Gong attacked Feng, could not capture it.

units.zh: 沛公還之沛，怨雍齒與豐子弟畔之。
units.en: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resentful that Yong Chi and the young men of Feng had rebelled against him.
units.literal: Pei Gong returned to Pei, resented Yong Chi and the Feng youths rebelling against him.

units.zh: 沛公往從之，道得張良，遂與俱見景駒，請兵以攻豐。
units.en: Pei Gong went to join him, met Zhang Liang along the way, and together they went to see Jing Ju, requesting troops to attack Feng.
units.literal: Pei Gong went to follow them, on the road obtained Zhang Liang, then together went to see Jing Ju, requested troops to attack Feng.

units.zh: 東陽甯君、沛公引兵西，與戰蕭西，不利，還收兵聚留。
units.en: The Lord of Dongyang Ning and Pei Gong led troops west and battled west of Xiao, but were unsuccessful, so they retreated and gathered troops at Liu.
units.literal: Dongyang Ning Jun, Pei Gong led troops west, fought battle at Xiao west, unfavorable, returned gathered troops at Liu.

units.zh: 四月，項梁擊殺景駒、秦嘉，止薛，沛公往見之。
units.en: In the fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju and Qin Jia, then stopped at Xue. Pei Gong went to see him.
units.literal: Fourth month, Xiang Liang attacked and killed Jing Ju, Qin Jia, stopped at Xue, Pei Gong went to see him.

units.zh: 項梁益沛公卒五千人，五大夫將十人。
units.en: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops by five thousand men and ten generals of the rank of Grand Master.
units.literal: Xiang Liang increased Pei Gong's troops five thousand, Grand Master generals ten people.

units.zh: 沛公還，引兵攻豐，拔之。
units.en: Pei Gong returned and led troops to attack Feng, capturing it.
units.literal: Pei Gong returned, led troops to attack Feng, captured it.

units.zh: 六月，沛公如薛，與項梁共立楚懷王孫心為楚懷王。
units.en: In the sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue and together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as King Huai of Chu.
units.literal: Sixth month, Pei Gong went to Xue, together with Xiang Liang established Chu King Huai's grandson Xin as Chu King Huai.

units.zh: 沛公攻亢父。
units.en: Pei Gong attacked Kangfu.
units.literal: Pei Gong attacked Kang Fu.

units.zh: 沛公與項梁共救田榮，大破章邯東阿。
units.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Liang together went to rescue Tian Rong and greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'e.
units.literal: Pei Gong together with Xiang Liang rescued Tian Rong, greatly defeated Zhang Han at Dong'a.

units.zh: 田榮歸，沛公、項羽追北，至城陽，攻屠其城。
units.en: Tian Rong returned. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu pursued the defeated enemy north to Chengyang and attacked, massacring the population of the city.
units.literal: Tian Rong returned, Pei Gong, Xiang Yu pursued north, arrived at Chengyang, attacked and slaughtered its city.

units.zh: 沛公、項羽去攻定陶。
units.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.
units.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu left to attack Dingtao.

units.zh: 定陶未下，沛公與項羽西略地至雍丘，與秦軍戰，大敗之，斬三川守李由。
units.en: Dingtao had not yet fallen. Pei Gong and Xiang Yu marched west to seize territory as far as Yongqiu, where they battled Qin troops and greatly defeated them, beheading the governor of Sanchuan, Li You.
units.literal: Dingtao not yet fallen, Pei Gong together with Xiang Yu west conquered territory to Yongqiu, fought with Qin army, greatly defeated them, beheaded Sanchuan defender Li You.

units.zh: 沛公、項羽方攻陳留，聞梁死，士卒恐，乃與將軍呂臣引兵而東，徙懷王自盱台都彭城。
units.en: Pei Gong and Xiang Yu were attacking Chenliu when they heard of Liang's death. The soldiers were terrified, so they joined with General Lü Chen and led troops east, moving King Huai from Xutai to Pengcheng as the capital.
units.literal: Pei Gong, Xiang Yu just attacking Chenliu, heard Liang died, soldiers afraid, then together with general Lu Chen led troops east, moved King Huai from Xutai capital to Pengcheng.

units.zh: 呂臣軍彭城東，項羽軍彭城西，沛公軍碭。
units.en: Lü Chen's army was stationed east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, and Pei Gong's army at Dang.
units.literal: Lu Chen's army east of Pengcheng, Xiang Yu's army west of Pengcheng, Pei Gong's army at Dang.

units.zh: 以沛公為碭郡長，封武安侯，將碭郡兵。
units.en: He appointed Pei Gong as governor of Dang commandery, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wuan, and put him in command of Dang commandery troops.
units.literal: Made Pei Gong Dang commandery chief, sealed as Marquis of Wuan, led Dang commandery troops.

units.zh: 獨羽怨秦破項梁，奮勢，願與沛公西入關。
units.en: Only Xiang Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang and was eager to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.
units.literal: Only Yu resented Qin for defeating Xiang Liang, exerted his influence, wished to go west into the pass with Pei Gong.

units.zh: 項羽不可遣，獨沛公素寬大長者。」
units.en: Xiang Yu should not be sent. Only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and an elder."
units.literal: Xiang Yu cannot be sent, only Pei Gong is habitually magnanimous and elder.'

units.zh: 卒不許羽，而遣沛公西收陳王、項梁散卒。
units.en: In the end they did not permit Xiang Yu, but sent Pei Gong west to gather the scattered troops of King Chen and Xiang Liang.
units.literal: In the end did not permit Yu, instead sent Pei Gong west to gather King Chen, Xiang Liang's scattered troops.

units.zh: 沛公攻破東郡尉於成武。
units.en: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dong commandery commandant at Chengwu.
units.literal: Pei Gong attacked and defeated the Dongjun prefect at Chengwu.

units.zh: 十二月，沛公引兵至栗，遇剛武侯，奪其軍四千餘人，并之，與魏將皇欣、武滿軍合，攻秦軍，破之。
units.en: In the twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li and encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized over four thousand of his men, and combined them. He joined with Wei generals Huang Xin and Wu Man's army and attacked Qin troops, defeating them.
units.literal: Twelfth month, Pei Gong led troops to Li, encountered Gangwu Marquis, seized his army more than four thousand people, merged them, combined with Wei generals Huang Xin, Wu Man armies, attacked Qin army, defeated it.

units.zh: 二月，沛公從碭北攻昌邑，遇彭越。
units.en: In the second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi and encountered Peng Yue.
units.literal: Second month, Pei Gong from north of Dang attacked Changyi, encountered Peng Yue.

units.zh: 沛公西過高陽，酈食其為里監門，曰：「諸將過此者多，吾視沛公大度。」
units.en: Pei Gong passed west through Gaoyang. Li Yiji was the village gatekeeper and said: "Many generals have passed through here. I can see that Pei Gong has great magnanimity."
units.literal: Pei Gong west passed Gaoyang, Li Yiji was village gatekeeper, said: 'Various generals who passed this place many, I observe Pei Gong has great magnanimity.'

units.zh: 乃求見沛公。
units.en: So he sought to see Pei Gong.
units.literal: Then requested to see Pei Gong.

units.zh: 沛公方踞床，使兩女子洗。
units.en: Pei Gong was sitting cross-legged on a bed, having two women wash his feet.
units.literal: Pei Gong just then squatting on bed, made two women wash.

units.zh: 於是沛公起，攝衣謝之，延上坐。
units.en: So Pei Gong rose, straightened his clothes, and apologized. He invited him to sit in the honored position.
units.literal: Thereupon Pei Gong rose, gathered clothes thanked him, invited to upper seat.

units.zh: 食其說沛公襲陳留。
units.en: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.
units.literal: Yiji persuaded Pei Gong to attack Chenliu by surprise.

units.zh: 沛公以為廣野君，以其弟商為將，將陳留兵。
units.en: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.
units.literal: Pei Gong made him Lord Guangye and appointed his younger brother Shang as general, commanding the Chenliu troops.

units.zh: 時趙別將司馬卬方欲渡河入關，沛公乃北攻平陰，絕河津。
units.en: At this time, Sima Ang, a separate Zhao general, was about to cross the Yellow River and enter the passes. Pei Gong therefore attacked Pingyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.
units.literal: At this time, the Zhao general Sima Ang was about to cross the river into the passes. Pei Gong attacked Beiyin to the north and cut off the river crossings.

units.zh: 沛公引兵過宛西。
units.en: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.
units.literal: Pei Gong led his troops west past Wan.

units.zh: 張良諫曰：「沛公雖欲急入關，秦兵尚眾，距險。
units.en: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.
units.literal: Zhang Liang advised: "Although Pei Gong wishes to rush into the passes, the Qin troops are still numerous and hold the dangerous passes.

units.zh: 沛公至霸上。
units.en: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.
units.literal: The Duke of Pei reached Bashang.

units.zh: 諸將或言誅秦王，沛公曰：「始懷王遣我，固以能寬容，且人已服降，殺之不祥。」
units.en: Some of the generals said that the King of Qin should be executed. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient. Moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered; to kill him would be inauspicious."
units.literal: Some of the generals said to execute the King of Qin. The Duke of Pei said, "When King Huai first sent me, it was precisely because I was able to be lenient; moreover, the man has already submitted and surrendered, and to kill him would be inauspicious."

units.zh: 三月，漢王自臨晉渡河，魏王豹降，將兵從。
units.en: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.
units.literal: In the third month, King Han crossed the Yellow River from Linjin. King Wei Bao surrendered and led troops to follow him.

units.zh: 南渡平陰津，至洛陽，新城三老董公遮說漢王曰：「臣聞『順德者昌，逆德者亡』，『兵出無名，事故不成』。
units.en: He crossed south at Pingyin Ford and reached Luoyang. Dong Gong, the elder of Xincheng, stopped the King of Han and advised him: "I have heard, 'Those who follow virtue prosper; those who oppose virtue perish,' and, 'When troops are sent out without a proper name, the enterprise will not succeed.'
units.literal: He crossed south at Pingyin ford and reached Luoyang. The elder of Xincheng, Dong Gong, blocked and advised King Han: "I have heard that 'those who follow virtue prosper, those who oppose virtue perish,' and 'when troops are sent out without just cause, affairs will not succeed.'

units.zh: 羽見紀信，問：「漢王安在？」
units.en: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"
units.literal: Xiang Yu saw Ji Xin and asked: "Where is King Han?"

units.zh: 漢王從之。
units.en: King Han followed their advice.
units.literal: King Han followed their advice.

units.zh: 吾與諸侯約，先入關者王之，吾當王關中。
units.en: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.
units.literal: I made an agreement with the feudal lords: whoever first entered the Pass would be king there, and I should be king in Guanzhong.

units.zh: 民又益喜，唯恐沛公不為秦王。
units.en: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.
units.literal: The people were even more delighted and feared only that the Duke of Pei would not become King of Qin.

units.zh: 背約，更立沛公為漢王，王巴、蜀、漢中四十一縣，都南鄭。
units.en: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.
units.literal: Breaking the agreement, he further established Pei Gong as King of Han, ruling Ba, Shu, Hanzhong, and 41 counties, with capital at Nanzheng.

units.zh: 漢王怨羽之背約，欲攻之，丞相蕭何諫，乃止。
units.en: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.
units.literal: King Han resented Xiang Yu for breaking the agreement and wanted to attack him. Chancellor Xiao He advised against it, so he stopped.

units.zh: 漢王曰：「善，非夫子無所聞。」
units.en: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."
units.literal: King Han said: "Excellent. Were it not for you, sir, I would have heard nothing of this."

units.zh: 及壯，試吏，為泗上亭長，廷中吏無所不狎侮。
units.en: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official and became pavilion chief of Sishang. Among the officials at court there was none he did not treat with familiar disrespect.
units.literal: When he reached adulthood, he tried serving as an official, became the pavilion chief of Sishang, and among the officials in the court there was none he did not treat with familiarity and insult.

units.zh: 沛公然其計，從之。
units.en: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.
units.literal: Pei Gong approved this plan and followed it.

units.zh: 五月，漢王引兵從故道出襲雍。
units.en: In the fifth month, King Han led troops from the old road to attack Yong by surprise.
units.literal: In the fifth month, King Han led troops from the old road to attack Yong by surprise.

units.zh: 漢王出滎陽，至成皋。
units.en: King Han left Xingyang and reached Chenggao.
units.literal: King Han left Xingyang and reached Chenggao.

units.zh: 母媼嘗息大澤之陂，夢與神遇。
units.en: Once, while resting by the dike of a vast marsh, his mother dreamed that she encountered a divine being.
units.literal: His mother the old woman once rested by the dike of the great marsh, and dreamed of encountering a god.

units.zh: 是時雷電晦冥，父太公往視，則見交龍於上。
units.en: At that moment, thunder crashed and darkness fell. His father, Taigong, went to investigate and saw two dragons entwined in the sky above.
units.literal: At this time thunder and lightning were dark and obscure, father Taigong went to look, then saw two dragons entwining above.

units.zh: 呂公女即呂后也，生孝惠帝、魯元公主。
units.en: This daughter of Lü Gong would become Empress Lü. She gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.
units.literal: Lü Gong's daughter was namely Empress Lü, gave birth to Emperor Xiaohui and Princess Lu Yuan.

units.zh: 呂后與兩子居田中，有一老父過請飲，呂后因餔之。
units.en: Empress Lü lived in the countryside with their two children. An old man passed by and asked for a drink. Empress Lü fed him.
units.literal: Empress Lü and the two children resided in the fields, there was an old father who passed by requesting drink, Empress Lü because of this fed him.

units.zh: 孝文皇帝，高祖中子也，母曰薄姬。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowen was the middle son of Emperor Gaozu, born to Lady Bo.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was Gaozu's middle son, his mother was named Lady Bo.

units.zh: 贊曰：孝文皇帝即位二十三年，宮室苑囿車騎服御無所增益。
units.en: The commentator states: Emperor Xiaowen reigned for twenty-three years without adding to the palaces, parks, carriages, horses, or furnishings.
units.literal: The commentator says: Emperor Xiaowen ascended the throne for twenty-three years, and the palaces, parks, carriages, horses, and furnishings were not increased at all.

units.zh: 高祖十一年，誅陳豨，定代地，立為代王，都中都。
units.en: In the eleventh year of Emperor Gaozu's reign, after executing Chen Xi and pacifying the Dai region, he was established as King of Dai with his capital at Zhongdu.
units.literal: In Gaozu's eleventh year, executed Chen Xi, pacified Dai territory, established as King of Dai, capital at Zhongdu.

units.zh: 皇帝即日夕入未央宮。
units.en: The emperor entered Weiyang Palace that same evening.
units.literal: That evening the emperor entered Weiyang Palace.

units.zh: 遂即天子位。
units.en: He immediately ascended the imperial throne.
units.literal: He then immediately ascended the imperial throne.

units.zh: 七年夏六月己亥，帝崩于未央宮。
units.en: On the day Jihai in the sixth month of summer in the seventh year, the emperor passed away in Weiyang Palace.
units.literal: In the seventh year, summer, sixth month, day Jihai, the emperor died in Weiyang Palace.

units.zh: 上曰： 「楚王，季父也，春秋高，閱天下之義理多矣，明於國家之體。
units.en: The emperor replied: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. Advanced in years and experienced in the world's moral principles, he understands the proper order of the state.
units.literal: The emperor said: 'The King of Chu is my uncle. He is advanced in age, has seen much of the world's principles and righteousness, understands the structure of the state.

units.zh: 吳王於朕，兄也；
units.en: The King of Wu is like an elder brother to me;
units.literal: The King of Wu is an elder brother to me;

units.zh: 淮南王，弟也：皆秉德以陪朕，豈為不豫哉！
units.en: The King of Huainan is like a younger brother to me. All of them uphold virtue to support me—how could they not stand ready as successors!
units.literal: The King of Huainan is my younger brother: all uphold virtue to assist me, how could they not be prepared!

units.zh: 子啟最長，敦厚慈仁，請建以為太子。」
units.en: Prince Qi is the eldest son, honest and sincere, kind and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'
units.literal: Prince Qi is the eldest, honest, kind, and benevolent. We petition to establish him as crown prince.'

units.zh: 皇太后曰：「立太子母竇氏為皇后。」
units.en: The Empress Dowager declared: 'Establish Lady Dou, mother of the crown prince, as empress.'
units.literal: The Empress Dowager said: 'Establish the crown prince's mother Lady Dou as empress.'

units.zh: 因立皇子武為代王，參為太原王，揖為梁王。
units.en: As a result, he established his sons Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.
units.literal: Consequently he established the imperial princes Wu as King of Dai, Can as King of Taiyuan, and Yi as King of Liang.

units.zh: 身衣弋綈，所幸慎夫人衣不曳地，帷帳無文繡，以示敦朴，為天下先。
units.en: He himself wore coarse silk garments, and his favored Lady Shen's robes did not trail on the ground. The curtains and canopies lacked embroidered patterns, demonstrating frugality and setting an example for the world.
units.literal: He himself wore coarse silk, and the favored Lady Shen's robes did not drag on the ground; the curtains and canopies had no embroidered patterns, to demonstrate frugality and lead the world by example.

units.zh: 孝文時，吳太子入見，得侍皇太子飲博。
units.en: In Emperor Wen’s reign the crown prince of Wu attended court and was allowed to drink and play liubo with the imperial heir.
units.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen the Wu heir came to court and was admitted to drink and play liubo with the heir apparent.

units.zh: 博爭道，不恭，皇太子引博局提吳太子，殺之。
units.en: They quarreled over the rules; the Wu heir showed disrespect, and the crown prince seized the heavy board and struck him dead.
units.literal: A dispute over a move in the game turned disrespectful; the imperial heir snatched up the gaming board and dashed it against the Wu prince, killing him.

units.zh: 朝錯為太子家令，得幸皇太子，數從容言吳過可削。
units.en: Chao Cuo was serving as household steward to the crown prince and had won his favor. He repeatedly said in private that Wu's offenses gave grounds for reducing its territory.
units.literal: Chao Cuo served as household steward to the crown prince. Favored by the crown prince, he repeatedly said in private that Wu's offenses could be grounds for reducing its territory.

units.zh: 及景帝即位，錯為御史大夫，說上曰：「昔高帝初定天下，昆弟少，諸子弱，大封同姓，故孽子悼惠王王齊七十二城，庶弟元王王楚四十城，兄子王吳五十餘城。
units.en: When Emperor Jing came to the throne, Chao Cuo became Imperial Counselor. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, he had few brothers and his sons were young, so he gave large fiefs to men of his own surname. Thus King Daohui, his son by a concubine, ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; King Yuan, his younger half-brother, ruled Chu with forty cities; and his nephew ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing took the throne, Cuo became Grandee Secretary. He urged the emperor, "When Gaozu first settled the realm, his brothers were few and his sons were young, so he made large grants to men of his own surname. Thus King Daohui, his son by a concubine, ruled Qi with seventy-two cities; King Yuan, his younger half-brother, ruled Chu with forty cities; and his elder brother's son ruled Wu with more than fifty cities.

units.zh: 孝景前三年正月甲子，初起兵於廣陵。
units.en: On jiǎzǐ in the first month of Xiaojing’s third year the rebellion opened at Guangling.
units.literal: On the jiǎzǐ day of the first month in the third year of Emperor Xiaojing, he first raised troops at Guangling.

units.zh: 七國反書聞，天子乃遣太尉條侯周亞夫將三十六將軍往擊吳楚；
units.en: News of the seven kingdoms’ revolt reached court; the emperor sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu of Tiaohou with thirty-six generals against Wu and Chu;
units.literal: When word of the seven states' rebellion reached the throne, the Son of Heaven dispatched Grand Commandant Marquis of Tiaohou Zhou Yafu with thirty-six generals to strike Wu and Chu;

units.zh: 陛下多病志逸，不能省察。
units.en: The Son of Heaven is sick in body and distracted in will; he cannot see through the plot.
units.literal: The sovereign is often ill in mind and body and cannot look into these matters.

units.zh: 二月，吳王兵既破，敗走，於是天子制詔將軍：「蓋聞為善者天報以福，為非者天報以殃。
units.en: In the second month Wu’s army was shattered; the emperor told his generals: “Heaven crowns virtue with fortune and strikes evil with woe.
units.literal: In the second month the King of Wu's army had already been broken and fled in defeat; the Son of Heaven then issued an edict to the generals: “We have heard that Heaven rewards the good with blessing and the wicked with calamity.

units.zh: 王頓首膝行對曰：「今者，朝錯天子用事臣，變更高皇帝法令，侵奪諸侯地。
units.en: On his knees Ang said, “Chao Cuo rules the court, rewrites Gaozu’s statutes, and gnaws at princely fiefs.
units.literal: The king, knocking his head and crawling on his knees, replied, “At present Chao Cuo is the minister in charge at the Son of Heaven's side; he has altered the laws of the August Emperor Gaozu and seized the princes' lands.

units.zh: 又使使愬條侯於上，上使告條侯救梁，又守便宜不行。
units.en: They complained to the throne; the emperor told him to relieve Liang, yet he clung to his plan and stayed put.
units.literal: They also sent envoys to denounce Zhou Yafu to the emperor; the emperor ordered him to save Liang, yet he still held to tactical advantage and did not move.

units.zh: 及後使人為秋請，上復責問吳使者。
units.en: Later, when Wu sent an envoy for the autumn audience, the emperor again questioned and rebuked him.
units.literal: Later, when Wu sent a man for the autumn audience, the emperor again questioned and rebuked the Wu envoy.

units.zh: 於是天子皆赦吳使者歸之，而賜吳王几杖，老，不朝。
units.en: The Son of Heaven pardoned the envoys and sent them back, then gave the king of Wu a folding stool and staff in token of old age, freeing him from court calls.
units.literal: The emperor pardoned Wu’s envoys and sent them home, then bestowed on the king of Wu an arm-rest and staff as tokens of age, exempting him from court attendance.

units.zh: 遣曲周侯酈寄擊趙，將軍欒布擊齊，大將軍竇嬰屯滎陽監齊趙兵。
units.en: he sent Li Ji, marquis of Quzhou, against Zhao and Luan Bu against Qi, while Grand General Dou Ying encamped at Xingyang to keep watch over the armies of Qi and Zhao.
units.literal: he sent Marquis Li Ji of Quzhou against Zhao and General Luan Bu against Qi; Grand General Dou Ying encamped at Xingyang to keep watch over the Qi and Zhao armies.

units.zh: 上從其議，遂斬錯。
units.en: The emperor accepted his counsel and had Chao Cuo executed.
units.literal: The emperor accepted his counsel and had Chao Cuo executed.

units.zh: 高皇帝親垂功德，建立諸侯，幽王、悼惠王絕無後，孝文皇帝哀憐加惠，王幽王子遂，悼惠王子卬等，令奉其先王宗廟，為漢藩國，德配天地，明並日月。
units.en: Gaozu established the kingdoms. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off, Emperor Wen compassionately made You’s son Sui, Daohui’s son Ang, and others kings so that they could tend their forefathers’ shrines and serve as Han’s outer bulwarks. His virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.
units.literal: The August Emperor Gaozu personally bestowed merit and virtue by establishing the princes. When the lines of King You of Zhao and King Daohui of Qi had been cut off without successors, Emperor Xiaowen took pity and extended his grace, making King You's son Sui, King Daohui's son Ang, and others kings so that they could maintain their forefathers' ancestral temples and serve as Han's outer bulwarks—his virtue matched Heaven and Earth, and his brilliance equaled the sun and moon.

units.zh: 而吳王濞背德反義，誘受天下亡命罪人，亂天下幣，稱疾不朝二十餘年。
units.en: Yet Liu Bi spurned virtue, drew in fugitives, disrupted the currency, and for more than twenty years pleaded illness and stayed away from court.
units.literal: Yet the King of Wu Liu Bi turned his back on virtue and violated righteousness, enticed and harbored fugitive criminals from the realm, threw the realm's currency into confusion, and for more than twenty years claimed illness and did not attend court.

units.zh: 有司數請濞罪，孝文皇帝寬之，欲其改行為善。
units.en: Officials begged his head; Wendi spared him, hoping he would mend his ways.
units.literal: The authorities repeatedly requested Bi's punishment; Emperor Xiaowen was lenient and wished him to change his conduct for the good.

units.zh: 今乃與楚王戊、趙王遂、膠西王卬、濟南王辟光、菑川王賢、膠東王雄渠約從謀反，為逆無道，起兵以危宗廟，賊殺大臣及漢使者，迫劫萬民，伐殺無罪，燒殘民家，掘其丘壟，甚為虐暴。
units.en: Now he has allied with Liu Wu of Chu, Liu Sui of Zhao, Liu Ang of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang of Jinan, Liu Xian of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong to plot rebellion. These lawless traitors menace the temples, murder ministers and envoys, coerce the people, kill the innocent, burn their homes, and dig open their graves. Their cruelty is monstrous.
units.literal: Now he has joined with Liu Wu, king of Chu, Liu Sui, king of Zhao, Liu Ang, king of Jiaoxi, Liu Piguang, king of Jinan, Liu Xian, king of Zichuan, and Liu Xiongqu, king of Jiaodong, in an alliance to plot rebellion. Lawless in their treason, they raised troops to endanger the ancestral temples, murdered great ministers and Han envoys, coerced the people, slaughtered the innocent, burned commoners' homes, and dug open their tombs—utterly cruel and violent.

units.zh: 而卬等又重逆無道，燒宗廟，鹵御物，朕甚痛之。
units.en: Ang’s crew have burned the shrines and plundered the palace stores—Our heart is torn.
units.literal: Yet Ang and the others have again been utterly lawless, burned the temples, looted the imperial gear—the pain of this is great in Us.

units.zh: 朕素服避正殿，將軍其勸士大夫擊反虜。
units.en: We wear mourning and quit the main hall—generals, drive your men at the traitors.
units.literal: We have donned plain dress and avoided the main hall; generals, urge your officers to strike the rebels.

units.zh: 擊反虜者，深入多殺為功，斬首捕虜比三百石以上皆殺，無有所置。
units.en: Advance deep and kill many to earn merit; execute every captured rebel of three-hundred-picul rank or higher, sparing none.
units.literal: Those who strike the rebels shall take deep advances and heavy killing as merit; every captured rebel of the three-hundred-picul rank or above shall be put to death, with none spared.

units.zh: 敢有議詔及不如詔者，皆要斬。」
units.en: Debate the decree or disobey it—death by waist chop.”
units.literal: Whoever dares debate the edict or fail to match the edict—waist cut in two.”

units.zh: 老父相后曰：「夫人天下貴人也。」
units.en: The old man read Empress Lü's face and said: "Madame, you are a noble person of the world."
units.literal: The old father read Empress Lü's face and said: "Madame is a noble person of the world."

units.zh: 審食其從太公、呂后間行，反遇楚軍，羽常置軍中以為質。
units.en: Shen Yiji escorted the Venerable Sire and Empress Lü along hidden paths, but they encountered Chu troops. Xiang Yu kept them with the army as hostages.
units.literal: Shen Yiji secretly escorted the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü, but encountered Chu troops. Xiang Yu constantly kept them in the army as hostages.

units.zh: 呂后兄周呂侯將兵居下邑，漢王往從之。
units.en: Empress Lü's elder brother Zhou Lühou led troops stationed at Xiayi. King Han went to join him.
units.literal: Empress Lü's elder brother Zhou Lühou led troops stationed at Xiayi. King Han went to join him.

units.zh: 九月，歸太公、呂后，軍皆稱萬歲。
units.en: In the ninth month, he returned the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü. The army all shouted ten thousand years.
units.literal: In the ninth month, he returned the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü. The army all shouted ten thousand years.

units.zh: 九月，漢王遣將軍薛歐、王吸出武關，因王陵兵，從南陽迎太公、呂后於沛。
units.en: In the ninth month, the King of Han sent Generals Xue Ou and Wang Xi out through Wuguan to join Wang Ling's troops and proceed from Nanyang to Pei to escort the Venerable Sire and Empress Lü.
units.literal: In the ninth month, King Han sent generals Xue Ou and Wang Xi out of Wuguan, relying on Wang Ling's troops, going from Nanyang to welcome the Duke of Tai and Empress Lü from Pei.

units.zh: 酒罷，呂媼怒呂公曰：「公始常欲奇此女，與貴人。
units.en: After the wine ended, Lü Po angrily confronted Lü Gong: "You always said this daughter was exceptional and should marry someone noble.
units.literal: The wine ended, Lü Po became angry at Lü Gong and said: "You at first constantly wished to treat this daughter as exceptional, to match her with a noble person.

units.zh: 文略嘗大遺魏收金，請為其父作佳傳，收論尒朱榮比韋、彭、伊、霍，蓋由是也。
units.en: Wenlüe once paid Wei Shou heavily to glorify his father in print—hence Shou’s likening of Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang.
units.literal: Wenlüe once gave Wei Shou a large gift of gold and asked him to write a fine biography of his father; that Wei Shou compared Erzhu Rong to Wei Qing, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Huo Guang was largely for this reason.

units.zh: 秦二世元年秋七月，陳涉起蘄，至陳，自立為楚王，遣武臣、張耳、陳餘略趙地。
units.en: In the first year of the Second Emperor of Qin, in autumn, in the seventh month, Chen She rose at Qi. He reached Chen, set himself up as King of Chu, and sent Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to seize the territory of Zhao.
units.literal: In the first year of the Second Emperor of Qin, in autumn, in the seventh month, Chen She rose at Qi, reached Chen, set himself up as King of Chu, and sent Wu Chen, Zhang Er, and Chen Yu to seize the territory of Zhao.

units.zh: 郡縣多殺長吏以應涉。
units.en: Many commanderies and counties killed their senior officials in response to Chen She.
units.literal: Many commanderies and counties killed their senior officials in order to respond to Chen She.

units.zh: 陳涉之將周章西入關，至戲，秦將章邯距破之。
units.en: Chen She's general Zhou Zhang marched west into the pass and reached Xi, where Qin general Zhang Han opposed and defeated him.
units.literal: Chen Sheng's general Zhou Zhang entered the pass westward, arrived at Xi, Qin general Zhang Han resisted and defeated him.

units.zh: 十二月，楚王陳涉為其御莊賈所殺。
units.en: In the twelfth month, King Chen She of Chu was killed by his charioteer Zhuang Jia.
units.literal: Twelfth month, Chu King Chen Sheng was killed by his charioteer Zhuang Jia.

units.zh: 且楚數進取，前陳王、項梁皆敗，不如更遣長者扶義而西，告諭秦父兄。
units.en: Moreover, Chu has repeatedly advanced but the former King Chen and Xiang Liang both failed. It would be better to send an elder who upholds righteousness to go west and inform the fathers and brothers of Qin.
units.literal: Moreover Chu repeatedly advanced and took, previously King Chen, Xiang Liang all defeated, not as good as again send elder who upholds righteousness west, inform and persuade Qin fathers and elder brothers.

units.zh: 周朝優詔答曰：「昔主父從戮，孔車有長者之風，彭越就誅，欒布得陪臣之禮。
units.en: Zhou replied graciously: "When Zhufu Yan was executed, Kong Che showed an elder's bearing; when Peng Yue was put to death, Luan Bu received a subject's rites.
units.literal: The Zhou court replied with a gracious edict, saying: "In old times when Zhufu Yan followed execution, Kong Che had an elder's bearing; when Peng Yue met execution, Luan Bu received a subject's rites.

units.zh: 布弟季心氣蓋關中，遇人恭謹，為任俠，方數千里，士爭為死。
units.en: Ji Bu's younger brother Ji Xin overshadowed all Guanzhong in sheer force of character; in person he was courteous and restrained, yet as a knight-errant his reputation ran for a thousand miles, and fighting men vied to die for him.
units.literal: Bu's younger brother Ji Xin, spirit covering Guanzhong, meeting people was respectful and careful; as knight-errant, square several thousand li, gentlemen strove to die for him.

units.zh: 當是時，季心以勇，布以諾，聞關中。
units.en: In those days Guanzhong knew Ji Xin for his courage and Ji Bu for keeping his word.
units.literal: At this time, Ji Xin by bravery, Bu by promise, were heard of in Guanzhong.

units.zh: 嘗為中司馬，中尉郅都不敢加。
units.en: He served as a marshal of the center; even Commandant Zhi Du would not touch him.
units.literal: He once was middle marshal; Commandant Zhi Du did not dare apply pressure.

units.zh: 嘗殺人，亡吳，從爰絲匿，長事爰絲，弟畜灌夫、籍福之屬。
units.en: After killing a man he fled to Wu and hid with Yuan Ang, whom he treated as an elder while treating Guan Fu, Ji Fu, and their like as younger brothers.
units.literal: He once killed a man, fled to Wu, followed Yuan Ang in hiding, served Yuan Ang as elder, and treated Guan Fu, Ji Fu, and their sort as younger brothers.

units.zh: 上問諸將，滕公言故楚令尹薛公有籌策。
units.en: The emperor asked the generals. Teng Gong spoke of the former Chu prime minister Xue Gong who had strategy.
units.literal: The emperor asked the generals. Teng Gong spoke of the former Chu prime minister Xue Gong who had strategy.

units.zh: 群臣袁盎等諫說雖切，常假借納用焉。
units.en: His ministers Yuan Ang and others offered blunt remonstrances, but he always accepted and employed them through tactful accommodation.
units.literal: His ministers Yuan Ang and others offered remonstrances that were cutting, but he always accepted and employed them through accommodation.

units.zh: 布母弟丁公，為項羽將，逐窘高祖彭城西。
units.en: Ji Bu's maternal uncle Ding Gong, a general under Xiang Yu, had pressed Gaozu hard west of Pengcheng.
units.literal: Ji Bu's maternal uncle Ding Gong, being Xiang Yu's general, pursued and cornered Gaozu west of Pengcheng.

units.zh: 及項王滅，丁公謁見高祖，以丁公徇軍中，曰：「丁公為項王臣不忠，使項王失天下者也。」
units.en: After Xiang Yu fell, Ding Gong came to pay his respects; Gaozu had him paraded before the host and declared, "Ding Gong was a faithless servant to his king; he helped cost Xiang Yu the empire."
units.literal: When King Xiang was destroyed, Ding Gong had audience with Gaozu; Gaozu had Ding Gong paraded before the army, saying, "Ding Gong as King Xiang's minister was not loyal; he is one who made King Xiang lose the empire."

units.zh: 善灌夫、鄭當時及宗正劉棄疾。
units.en: He counted Guan Fu, Zheng Dangshi, and the director of the imperial clan Liu Qiji among his friends.
units.literal: He was on good terms with Guan Fu, Zheng Dangshi, and Liu Qiji, director of the imperial clan.

units.zh: 僕有三罪，而欲求活，此伍子胥所以僨於吳世也。
units.en: With three crimes of my own, to seek life would be like Wu Zixu's downfall in Wu.
units.literal: With three crimes of my own, to seek life would be like Wu Zixu's ruin in Wu.

units.zh: 郅都、甯成之倫，猛氣奮發，摧拉凶邪，一切以救時弊。
units.en: Men such as Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, fierce in spirit, crushed the wicked by every means solely to remedy the disorders of their age.
units.literal: Men like Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, with fierce energy flourishing, crushed and pulled down the wicked—everything solely to remedy the ills of the times.

units.zh: 其禁奸除猾，殆與郅、寧之倫異乎。
units.en: Their suppression of treachery and elimination of villains was rather different from the likes of Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, was it not?
units.literal: Their suppression of treachery and elimination of cunning—this differed little from the class of Zhi and Ning.

units.zh: 漢革其風，矯枉過正，禁綱疏闊，遂漏吞舟。
units.en: The Han reformed that harshness but overcorrected: the prohibitory net grew so slack that even great offenders slipped through.
